The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 10th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

story.head: Rantanen’s favorite opponent
paras: The Stars won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-0 in Dallas on Oct 5. The Sharks (7-7-1) lost 5-1 to Ottawa on Oct 31, while the Stars (8-5-1) beat Columbus 3-1 the same night. The Sharks played last night, and the Stars are rested. Going in, the Sharks are fourth in the Pacific (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Stars fourth in the Central (tied for 13th).
The Sharks’ record (.500) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.367), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Stars’ record (.607) is about what their chances are worth.

The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest), are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). As for the Stars, they block more shots than anyone (1st) and play slow, tight games (lowest). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and that could do real damage against the Sharks’ penalty kill (27th). Dallas has allowed 2.14 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Stars keep shots away, but the Sharks give up plenty.

Macklin Celebrini (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 13 GP) is carrying the Sharks’ offense, and Will Smith (6 G / 4 A / 10 P in 15 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in eight straight games against San Jose. Jason Robertson (5 G / 9 A / 14 P in 14 GP) is next in line.
Alex Nedeljkovic (3-2-1 / .899 SV% in 6 GS) is in line to start for San Jose. Jake Oettinger (7-3-1 / .922 SV% in 11 GS) has been a rock in net for Dallas and will likely start.
The Stars usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.
